title: The Treatment of Iran’s World Cup Team Exposed the West's and FIFA's Double Standards
author: Fatima Bhutto
content:
When the Iranian football team left Los Angeles after their second match at
the 2026 World Cup, they left [behind a handwritten
note](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49142264/iran-thank-note-los-
angeles-world-cup-hospitality) in their locker room thanking the city for "its
hospitality." Iranian politeness is famous, but "hospitality" is not the word
that comes to mind when I think of how the Iranian national team has been
treated by FIFA and the United States, one of the World Cup's 2026 host
countries. Not only did President Donald Trump [welcome the
team](https://apnews.com/article/trump-world-cup-soccer-
iran-e122ed266115de6ff2b6a7d82e9a641a) back in March by saying that he did not
think the team's participation in the tournament was "appropriate," citing
possible dangers to their "lives and safety," but his administration also
denied as many visas as possible, [required the team to leave the
U.S.](https://apnews.com/article/iran-world-cup-complaint-
visas-8be2c56639a8ab0c464145710e912a09) immediately after every match, and
forced them to be based across the border in Mexico, initially
[allowing](https://www.npr.org/2026/06/24/g-s1-129820/irans-world-cup-travel-
restrictions) entry to the great United States only within 24 hours before a
match. When the Iranian national anthem played, as is customary, before their
two games in a Los Angeles Stadium, [parts of the crowd
booed](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/iran-star-addresses-fans-
booing-145124861.html?guccounter=1).

At every press conference, journalists who have spent careers lobbing
softballs at sportsmen made sure to quiz Iranian captain Mehdi Taremi as
obnoxiously as possible, asking him after the team's 1-1 draw against Egypt
whether he supports LGBT people. "We respect all of the LGBT people," Taremi
[answered](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/sports/fifa-world-cup-2026-we-
respect-all-of-lgbt-people-says-iran-skipper-taremi-after-pride-game-against-
egypt/), before wondering if the journalist had any questions about the actual
game of football that had been played. One can only assume that [Kylian
Mbappe](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49148833/france-star-kylian-
mbappe-fast-becoming-mr-world-cup), the French captain, was quizzed on
[Emmanuel Macron's](https://blogs.lse.ac.uk/europpblog/2026/02/06/france-debt-
crisis-macron-eurozone-stability/) stalling of the French economy, the
Austrian captain questioned about his country's love of [far-right
politicians](https://www.euractiv.com/news/boring-is-the-new-black-austrias-
risky-attempt-to-play-the-long-game/), and Argentina's team captain made to
answer about why [Javier Milei](https://apnews.com/article/javier-milei-
profile-argentina-election-82488d49cca5aee10d4b911bde530922) is such a weirdo.
They weren't. Was the U.S. captain asked about his country's funding of
Israel's genocide in Gaza, or its bombing of a girls' school that killed at
least [100 children in Minab](https://zeteo.com/p/100-days-and-still-no-
answers-for) on the first day of Trump's war on Iran? No? What a surprise.

I am old enough to remember when American celebrities and British pundits made
a hue and cry about Qatar hosting a World Cup.
